classification.difficultyReason: Combine e and 4e into the whole base, reverse the triangle-area formula to determine e, then use the two resulting base segments in separate Pythagoras calculations.

content.prompt: Calculate the unknown values to 1 d.p., given the area of the triangle is $2550\text{ mm}^{2}$.

spec.description: Tall unfilled triangle with apex slightly right of its left base endpoint. Sloping sides are labelled t and n. A dashed perpendicular height divides the horizontal base into e and 4e, with a right-angle marker at its foot.
spec.mathematics: Height 85 mm; base segments e and 4e. The two right triangles determine t and n after e is found from the total area.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown labels appear; calculated lengths remain in answer fields.

answer.short: $e=12.0\text{ mm},\quad t=85.8\text{ mm},\quad n=97.6\text{ mm}$. Use $2550=\frac{85\times5e}{2}$ to find $e$, then apply Pythagoras to each right triangle.
answer.worked:
The total base is $e+4e=5e$. Use the triangle-area formula, then Pythagoras in each right triangle.
$$\begin{align*}
2550&=\frac{85\times5e}{2}\\
2550&=\frac{425}{2}e\\
e&=12\text{ mm}\\
4e&=48\text{ mm}\\
t^{2}&=12^{2}+85^{2}\\
t&=\sqrt{7369}\text{ mm}\\
t&\approx85.8\text{ mm}\\
n^{2}&=48^{2}+85^{2}\\
n&=\sqrt{9529}\text{ mm}\\
n&\approx97.6\text{ mm}
\end{align*}$$
Thus $e=12.0\text{ mm}$ to 1 d.p.
